title: Time and Dates
summary: Working with time in standard C - time_t and time, breaking it into struct tm with gmtime and localtime, formatting with strftime, building and normalising dates with mktime, differences with difftime, measuring how long code takes with clock and timespec_get, and the pitfalls of time zones and thread safety.

cards.a:
January

Months in `struct tm` count from 0, so January is 0 and December is 11. Days of the month (`tm_mday`) start at 1.

cards.q: How can `mktime` help with "30 days after this date"?
cards.a:
Add 30 to `tm_mday` and call `mktime`; it normalises the date into the right month and year

`mktime` accepts out-of-range fields and fixes them up, so day 45 of a month becomes the right day of the next month, across years too.

cards.q: Which gives the time as text in ISO 8601 form?
cards.a:
`strftime(buf, sizeof buf, "%FT%T", t)`

strftime does the formatting; `%F` is `%Y-%m-%d` and `%T` is `%H:%M:%S`. printf does not understand `%Y`, and asctime and ctime use their own fixed layout.
